purpose: Teriparatide is used to treat osteoporosis, which is a condition where your bones become weak and fragile. It is typically prescribed for people who have a high risk of breaking a bone, such as those who have already had a fracture or have tried other osteoporosis medicines without enough benefit. It helps make your bones stronger and reduces your chance of fractures.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes a hormone called parathyroid hormone, which helps control how your bones are built and maintained. Teriparatide is a man-made version of part of that hormone, and when given as a daily injection, it actually stimulates your bone-forming cells to build new, stronger bone. Think of it like giving your bones a daily signal to grow and rebuild themselves.
common_side_effects: Some people feel dizzy or lightheaded, especially right after the injection, so it is best to sit or lie down for a few minutes afterward. You might also notice nausea, leg cramps, or mild pain at the injection site. Some people experience headaches or feel more tired than usual.
warnings: Teriparatide should not be used for more than 2 years total in your lifetime, as studies showed a rare risk of a bone tumor called osteosarcoma in animals given very high doses. It should not be used in people who have had radiation treatment to their bones, have high calcium levels (hypercalcemia), or have certain bone cancers. Talk to your doctor right away if you experience persistent back or bone pain, which could be a sign of a spinal fracture.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 20 micrograms injected just under the skin (subcutaneous injection) once a day. It comes as a pre-filled injection pen that you use yourself at home, and it is typically injected into the thigh or abdomen. Your doctor will show you exactly how to use it, and treatment is usually limited to no more than 2 years.
